קַשְׁתָּם is a bare accusative of comparison apposed to the object, and the ASV supplies the simile frame 'as it were' for it. The competing reading treats 'as it were' as a parenthetical hedge answering to no morpheme and marks it added, corroborated by the ASV italics; I took the rule 33 reading because the italics are evidence only (rule 7) and 'as' is exactly the function word an English comparison of a bare Hebrew accusative requires.

variant_decisions.evidence: ASV renders the phrase adjectivally as 'a deadly arrow', with no ASV note attached to this unit. 'Deadly' shows neither the passive voice of the qere participle shachut nor the active voice of the ketiv shochet; an arrow called deadly is equally one that slays (ketiv) and one that is sharpened/slaughtering-made (qere). No italicized supply and no other ASV wording in 9:8 bears on the participle's form, so the English permits both readings and the qere base fallback carries the projection.
